A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RAD research despite the refined title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across revisions.

before.justification: V1 reports original RAD benchmark results, few-shot and data-scaling experiments, encoder comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: V3 retains original empirical results and adds matched-backbone comparisons, sensitivity tests, unseen-normal analyses, efficiency measurements, and memory-compression results.

M1.justification: Section 5.6 introduces an evaluated coreset-compressed RAD variant, changing the stored feature memory. The main frozen-encoder, global retrieval, spatial conditioning, and multilayer cosine-scoring procedure remains unchanged. Explicit uniform fusion weights are newly disclosed rather than an established algorithm change.

E1.justification: V3 adds MVTec-AD2 evaluation in Appendix I and extends incremental-class evaluation to VisA, introducing macaroni1 alongside three fixed categories in Appendix L. This is a limited expansion within industrial anomaly detection; the original four benchmarks and RGB-only use of 3D-ADAM remain.

E2.justification: Table 1 adds GeneralAD to the standard comparisons. The 3D-ADAM comparison in Table A3 removes Uninet while retaining PatchCore and Dinomaly. The few-shot comparator membership remains unchanged; PatchCore is relocated and relabeled, not newly introduced.

E3.justification: The 3D-ADAM comparison upgrades Dinomaly to DINOv3 and expands reporting from two F1 metrics to seven metrics. V3 also introduces matched-backbone controls, explicit hyperparameter sweeps, FPR at 95% TPR evaluation, compression/latency comparisons, and VisA target-class scaling protocols. Background filtering is newly specified for 3D-ADAM; v1 does not establish its earlier filtering procedure.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component ablations and encoder/scaling studies, v3 adds tests separating backbone strength from retrieval, sensitivity to K/radius/fusion weights, unseen-normal generalization, 3D-ADAM score distributions, memory compression, retrieval latency, and incremental-class transfer to VisA. These substantially broaden the questions examined.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the seed=1 and deterministic-CUDA statement in Appendix A, without adding repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new score means and percentiles are distribution diagnostics rather than uncertainty estimates for experimental performance.

E6.justification: Table A3 replaces the 3D-ADAM results: RAD's image/pixel F1 changes from 92.6/32.5 to 96.4/46.4, and its image-level ranking changes. The upgraded comparator and newly specified filtering prevent interpreting this as an established same-setting gain. Substantial new results cover backbone controls, MVTec-AD2, sensitivity, false positives, efficiency, compression, and VisA scaling. Existing few-shot, scaling, encoder, and per-category scores are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix D adds Theorem D.3, defining expected anomaly–normal separation and proving a near-optimality bound controlled by unseen-normal distance to memory under a finite-expectation assumption. V1 already contained empirical saturation, pointwise maximality, and non-expansiveness results, which are retained. Section 3.4 additionally derives retrieval-complexity bounds.

C1.justification: V1 presents upper-bounding reconstruction residuals as a central theoretical contribution. V3 removes that broad claim and states maximality within a restricted class of stable scores instead. Its contribution list emphasizes mitigating cross-category/cross-region mismatches and comparisons with trained and training-free methods, while retaining the central RAD performance claim.

C2.justification: Appendix G shifts the explanation of low pixel F1 from background activations toward extreme anomaly-pixel imbalance and score-tail overlap. New discussions interpret backbone-controlled gains, unseen-normal memory coverage, hyperparameter robustness, and compression tradeoffs. V3 also removes the cross-dataset training/test-ratio argument for data efficiency from Section 5.2.

D1.justification: V3 explicitly specifies uniform fusion weights of 0.25 and official 3D-ADAM background filtering, and reports inference latency and memory requirements. Appendix A's preprocessing, retrieval parameters, software, hardware, and seed details remain unchanged, as does the code-access information. The new coreset variant lacks a detailed selection procedure.

R1.justification: V3 more explicitly positions RAD against existing training-free nearest-neighbor approaches and relabels PatchCore as training-free in Table A1. It adds references for deep nearest-neighbor detection, GeneralAD, MVTec-AD2, ImageNet, and two 3D anomaly-detection works. The extensive related-work review otherwise remains largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation and contributions, spatial-conditioning explanation, Section 4, and Appendix G undergo substantial rewriting. Task-specific training terminology is adopted throughout. New efficiency sections and diagnostic appendices reshape the exposition, with the former per-category and visualization appendices moved from I/J to M/N.

P2.justification: V3 adds six tables displaying compression, score distributions, backbone controls, sensitivity, unseen-normal generalization, and VisA scaling. Table A3 is redesigned from two F1 columns to seven metrics; Table A1 reorders PatchCore, and per-category tables are packed more tightly. Existing plots and qualitative images are retained and repositioned.

improvement.justification: V3 corrects an important overstatement by aligning the central theoretical claim with a restricted score class and adding a proved separation guarantee. Matched-backbone controls, unseen-normal and sensitivity tests, and measured resource tradeoffs substantially strengthen attribution and practical validation. The removed Uninet comparison and limited coreset implementation detail do not outweigh these gains; the improvement rests on stronger justification, not the higher replacement 3D-ADAM scores.
